reconcile.connective: Commentators read 'not yet given' as a change in degree, not the Spirit's first arrival, distinguishing Pentecost's effusion from his earlier presence in Zacharias and Elizabeth.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells (Skeptic's Annotated Bible) presses John 7:39's plain claim that the Spirit 'was not yet given' against six earlier verses of people already Spirit-filled.

skeptic.name: Steve Wells
skeptic.work: The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "When was the Holy Ghost given?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/ghost.html)
skeptic.attribution: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible (online; contra/ghost.html)

excerpts.excerpt_text: He was in the Old Testament prophets and saints, and Zacharias and Elisabeth were both filled with the Holy Ghost. This therefore must be understood of the eminent, plentiful, and general effusion of the Spirit which was promised, Joe 2:28, and accomplished, Act 2:1, etc.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves 'not yet given' against this contradiction's own OT-side prooftexts (Zacharias, Elisabeth), reading their Spirit-filling as a lesser degree than Pentecost's 'eminent, plentiful, general effusion.'

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874), p. 417-418
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley treats this contradiction directly under two adjacent entries: 'Holy Spirit bestowed before Pentecost. Not till that time' (John 20:22 vs. Acts 1:5,8; 2:1-4), quoting Alford that the breathing was 'a symbol and foretaste of what they should receive at Pentecost'; and immediately prior, an entry on John 7:39 resolving 'not yet given' by supplying the elided verb ('not yet [received by them]').

link.title: GotQuestions: What does it mean in John 20:22 that Jesus breathed on the disciples and said, "Receive the Holy Spirit"?
link.note: Live apologetic treatment of the John 20:22 vs. Acts 2 timing tension (temporary empowering/pledge vs. Pentecost's permanent indwelling).
